LESSON: WRITING 14.4.1 GUIDED WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.1: Writing 14.4.1 Guided writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 14.4.1 Guided writing, part of Strand 14 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we plan before writing a composition? 2. How do we learn to write fluently?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Pick out new words from a text based on the theme. Learners with speech difficulties can select orally, by typing or writing.

2. Write the new words correctly and legibly. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body, type or use assistive technology.

3. Write 3-5 meaningful sentences using the new words in response to a prompt,

4. Write own paragraphs of 3-5 sentences using the steps in the writing process. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Pick out new words from a text based on the theme. Learners with speech difficulties can select orally, by typing or writing.
2. Write the new words correctly and legibly. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools and materials, alternative functional parts of the body, type or use assistive technology.
3. Write 3-5 meaningful sentences using the new words in response to a prompt,
4. Write own paragraphs of 3-5 sentences using the steps in the writing process. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use adapted writing tools. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 14.4.1 Guided writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication: The learner’s ability to write clearly and legibly is enhanced as they write short narratives following the five

steps of the writing process.

 Creativity and Imagination: The learner’s originality skills are enhanced as they come up with unique and new ideas and use

them to write a narrative.

Values:
Responsibility is nurtured as the learner ensures that they develop organisation skills in preparation for independent writing.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s acquires an enhanced level self-esteem as their w r i t i n g s k i l l s i m p r o v e .

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner is able to apply the five steps of the writing process when writing paragraphs in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources:

Well written texts, assistive technology such as universal cuffs/wrist braces/arm braces, weighted pencil/pen grips, page-turners,

adapted digital devices
